A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hessian-free recollection method. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CelebA, including runtime measurements, sensitivity studies and repair validation.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional LFW and expanded CelebA evaluations, including accuracy, model distance and computational costs.

M1.justification: The affine-recursion approximator, HVP computation, vector-addition unlearning and optional repair strategy remain. However, Algorithms 1 and 2 change the stated gradient-rescaling operation from rescaling the batch-averaged gradient to rescaling individual gradients before averaging.

E1.justification: v3 adds LFWPeople face recognition across 29 identities. MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CelebA remain represented; Fashion-MNIST results move to the appendix. This is a limited extension within the existing vision evaluation.

E2.justification: FineTune and NegGrad join the CelebA comparison in v3 Table 5, whereas v1 Figure 3 compares the proposed method only with retraining. The NS/IJ comparisons on smaller models and the CIFAR-10 comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The large-model protocols change substantially. CelebA moves from 1,000 samples, 10 epochs, learning rate 0.05 and batch size 32 to 10,000 samples, 5 epochs, 0.01 and 64; deletion changes from 200 samples to 50. CIFAR-10 NegGrad changes from two epochs at 0.0001 with batch size 1 to one epoch at 0.00005 with batch size 2. v3 also specifies the new LFW protocol and adds distance measurements to application comparisons.

E4.justification: v3 removes the sequential deletion-and-repair validation from v1 Appendix C.2/Figure 7 while retaining the repair method. It also removes accuracy trajectories from the small-step-size and epoch studies and drops the step-size-1 results. These remove evidence about repair effectiveness and the utility consequences of hyperparameter choices, although the four principal distance-based sensitivity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report seven random seeds and minimum/maximum error bars for the principal verification experiments, and identify seed 42 for the sensitivity studies. v3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: CIFAR-10 Table 3 replaces several reported values, including the proposed method's distance of 0.09 with 0.06. v3 Tables 4–7 add LFW, expanded CelebA and resource/distance results; LFW accuracy is 71.92% versus 80.89% for retraining. Changed CelebA and NegGrad settings prevent interpreting their replacements as same-setting improvements. Figure 1(b)'s revised inset also shows about 0.68 at 30% deletion while the text retains 0.96.

T1.justification: v3 substantively revises existing guarantees rather than introducing generalization and deletion capacity for the first time. It revises the approximation-error normalization, changes the generalization term from rho^T 2ML/lambda to rho^T 2L^2/lambda, and changes the supporting contraction argument from SGD to GD. Appendix E.1 replaces Hessian-Lipschitz/asymptotic conditions with smoothness and empirical optimality, while Appendix B.6 adds a bound-tightness analysis.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds efficient online unlearning under less restrictive assumptions. v3 explicitly claims applicability to non-convex, non-smooth objectives and the first non-convex theoretical analysis of certified unlearning. Its abstract and conclusion also elevate superiority in generalization and deletion capacity to central contributions, while retaining the original efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's existing step-size discussion, v3 adds explicit limitations concerning O(nTd) precomputation, O(nd) storage and unstable non-convex training. It interprets the new LFW performance loss as an applicability limitation and discusses potentially loose bounds near rho = q. Appendix E.2 proposes grouped storage and sharpness-aware training as future remedies, not evaluated components.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendix B.1's detailed CNN architecture, numerical clipping thresholds and explicit experimental noise scale of 0.1. It adds settings for LFW and the revised large-model comparisons, and adds RTX 3090 to the hardware disclosure. The code URL, PyTorch/CUDA versions and CPU information remain, but important reproduction details are lost.

R1.justification: The new Appendix A substantially expands discussion of SISA, federated unlearning, influence functions, distillation and Fisher-based alternatives, with additional citations. Research positioning shifts toward theoretical certified unlearning and an explicit first-non-convex-analysis claim; new sharpness-aware minimization references support future directions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 4 places generalization analysis before algorithm design, the research-question framing is removed, and appendices are reorganized into separate related-work, proof, experiment, ablation and discussion sections. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and figures are redrawn or relocated. v1 Table 2 is redistributed across v3 Tables 2 and 6, with an added distance column in the latter. New large-model tables replace or expand earlier displays, while accuracy panels and the repair figure are removed.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluation, especially the LFW failure case, and explicit scalability limitations make v3 more informative. However, it removes important reproduction settings and repair validation, introduces a figure/text inconsistency, and strengthens nonsmooth-certification claims without clearly resolving their dependence on Hessians and Taylor expansions. These substantive benefits and unresolved reliability losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
